summary: Every clip above 350K locks a single sentence of on-screen text for the full duration — the text is the punchline, not a label for the footage. The top two (2.9M and 784K) both frame Lucia as a chaotic-but-lovable protagonist using soft Gen-Z internet language plus 1-2 crying/shocked emojis. Rank 4 (355K) confirms platform-envy and community-relatable memes convert strongly even after launch. Rank 6 (342K) proves a visual-showcase angle ('how I dress Lucia') with a slow outfit reveal across 3 shots hits almost as hard — the text stays static and minimal, letting the visuals do the escalation. The consistent separating factor between top and bottom performers is bright, well-lit footage with white sentence-case text readable from frame one; dark shots and fragmented multi-beat text consiste
moments_to_pick: Lucia doing something weirdly human or adorably chaotic in an idle or ambient animation — the smaller and more specific the detail, the stronger the 'wdym she really does this' reaction
Jason accidentally endangering or over-protecting Lucia — the tension between his loyalty and the game's chaos is the proven emotional hook at 784K
First-person player confessional about something funny, embarrassing, or emotional the player did to/with Lucia or Jason in one sentence ('I almost killed Lucia' format, proven at 784K)
Visual showcase: 3 shots of the same subject escalating — outfit changes, location beauty, or a detail that gets closer/more impressive each shot (proven at 342K with Lucia outfits)
Platform-envy or community-relatable jealousy meme — PC players waiting, people at work, anyone who can't play yet; universally self-insertable and proven at 355K
A single GTA 6 environment or animation detail shown across 3 bright daytime shots that escalates the 'this cannot be a video game' reaction

title_formula: Lead with the specific Lucia/Jason moment or player reaction in plain spoken language + one concrete detail (her name, an action, a location) + 1-2 emojis, under 60 characters. Pattern: '[What she/he/I did] [specific detail] [emoji]'. Examples: 'Lucia Really Walked Out Like That 😭✌️' or 'I Nearly Lo
caption_formula: One short sentence (under 12 words) that reframes the on-screen joke with a slight new angle or extra emotional beat — never copy the hook text word for word. Line break. '🎵 Tokyo Girl — Passive' (required song credit, always present). Line break. Hashtag block. Total under 150 characters excluding
avoid: Dark, low-contrast, or night-interior shots where white sentence text becomes unreadable — the single biggest performance killer visible across all ranked clips
Splitting the punchline across 3 separate text beats on the main clip — the 2.9M and 784K clips both hold ONE sentence the full clip; fragmented jokes lose the laugh before it lands
Any launch-date or countdown framing — the game is live and that reads as outdated immediately
Overly niche scenarios fewer than 60% of GTA fans can self-insert into (hyper-specific build choices, regional references, in-game UI screenshots without context)
Putting song credit or 'Tokyo Girl' anywhere in the on-screen text overlay — caption only per campaign rules
Any audio other than Tokyo Girl added in TikTok/IG — no voiceover, no dialogue, no game audio
